suggestions.description: The current implementation uses repetitive if-statements to map permission object properties to Permission Policy feature names. This creates maintenance burden as each new permission requires adding a new if-statement. The mapping between TypeScript property names and Permission Policy feature names (e.g., clipboardWrite → clipboard-write) is inconsistent and implicit.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates repetitive code (DRY principle), makes adding new permissions require only updating the map, centralizes the TypeScript-to-Policy-name mapping, reduces chance of errors when adding new permissions, makes transformation logic more declarative, and ensures type-safe mapping.

suggestions.description: As an alternative to the full declarative refactoring, extract the permission checking logic into a separate helper function to reduce duplication while maintaining linear flow.
suggestions.benefits: Reduces duplication in the conditional logic, makes the pattern more explicit, easier to test the permission-adding logic in isolation, and maintains a clear, linear flow that's easy to read.

refactorings.summary: The most significant refactoring opportunity exists in the buildAllowAttribute function. The current implementation uses repetitive if-statements that violate the DRY principle.
